editorial.marketOverview: US equities enter November 23–25 following Friday's unusually severe AI and semiconductor-led liquidation. Nasdaq and SOX historical losses, negative breadth and elevated fear readings indicate downside pressure. No Sunday US cash session has occurred and no Monday reaction can be claimed.
editorial.whatChanged: Reuters' November 22 weekend assessment identifies both a correction and possible oversold stabilization, reinforcing the existing two-sided risk rather than changing the direction. A reported VIX Friday close of 35.89 conflicts with an earlier 37.66 figure; it is flagged rather than silently replacing the prior observation. Open Watch's 174 curated events have not changed.
editorial.marketInterpretation: The relative collapse of semiconductors versus broad technology remains the most important bearish leadership signal. A short-covering bounce is plausible after sharp declines, but it is not equivalent to confirmed accumulation. Yields, yield-curve slope, Fed pricing and crude-oil inputs lack a fresh synchronized cross-asset set, limiting confidence in macro attribution.
editorial.threeDayPath: Monday: watch whether flash PMI and the first full cash session produce semiconductor stabilization or renewed selling. Tuesday: consumer confidence and ADI/DELL earnings can test AI infrastructure demand and market breadth. Wednesday: PCE/GDP and related macro releases may change yields and Fed expectations rapidly. The base case remains volatile downside risk with sharp countertrend rallies possible; catalyst effects are prospective.
editorial.bullCase: An oversold rebound becomes credible if QQQ, SOX and SMH advance together, breadth broadens, and both VXN and VIX retreat on matching timestamps. Constructive AI hardware guidance and benign inflation could reinforce that move, but none has yet been observed.
editorial.bearCase: Continued NVDA/SOX underperformance, narrow participation and persistent volatility would indicate Friday's liquidation has not cleared. A hotter PCE or hawkish rate repricing would add pressure to growth valuations; this is conditional, not a forecast of the release.
editorial.watchNext: Verify Monday cash-market QQQ/SOX/SMH breadth and VXN/VIX together; obtain primary Treasury 2Y/10Y yields and express their spread in basis points, CME FedWatch pricing, and contract-matched Brent/WTI. Monitor primary regulatory developments and ADI/DELL guidance. Treat all Friday prices as historical.
